findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "browse" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "list_item" is 3278 chars, far longer than this server's median (638). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: front_door, official_facts, browse, visit_store, read_listing, read_events, merchants, list_item, sync_world, world_status, buy, my_purchases, me · Private data: official_facts, list_item, list_world, sync_world, edit_item, buy, my_purchases, treasury · Public sink: official_facts, list_item, world_status, withdraw_item, comment, flag · Destructive: remove_listing.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: front_door, official_facts, browse, visit_store, read_listing, read_events, merchants, list_item, sync_world, world_status, buy, my_purchases, me · Private data: official_facts, list_item, list_world, sync_world, edit_item, buy, my_purchases, treasury · Public sink: official_facts, list_item, world_status, withdraw_item, comment, flag · Destructive: remove_listing

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "official_facts" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
